data.body:
CLOSE EVIDENCE — all five acceptance criteria re-verified against the MERGED tree, not against
my earlier working copy. Worktree HEAD == origin/main == d49fea41cc38; commit 50716c9aed87
("Describe the config-inspect tool that is pinned", Gerrit 2678) confirmed an ancestor of HEAD by
`git merge-base --is-ancestor`, and `rebar verify-commit-ticket --rev 50716c9aed87` resolves
f95d-19f6-7e58-4a8e. The audited binary was reinstalled from the pinned commit
2fb54c236733ee65ee877105d595c124c993c64d with Go 1.25.1 so every check below ran against the
REAL tool, not a fake.

AC1 — canary passes with the audited binary on PATH. MET.
  PATH=…:/tmp/tfci-bin REBAR_TERRAFORM_CONFIG_INSPECT_CANARY=1 \
    pytest tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py -k pinned_upstream_canary -q
  -> 1 passed, 24 deselected in 13.28s
  Pre-fix, identical command and identical binary: AssertionError: assert 'abstain' == 'match'
  (CI jobs 101295228786 on change 2674 and 101290520693 on the dependabot PR-merged tree).

AC2 — schema validates one real document, zero violations. MET.
  Scripted jsonschema `iter_errors` over one real `terraform-config-inspect --json .` document,
  validated against the merged src/rebar/schemas/terraform_config_inspect.schema.json:
  -> "schema violations against the real pinned binary: 0"   (it was 15 before the fix)

AC3 — `_run` passes "." and the child's cwd remains the snapshot; the no-leak assertion survives.
  MET.
  src/rebar/grounding/terraform_corroborator.py:292   [str(exe), "--json", "."],
  tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py:294  assert capture["argv"][1:] == ["--json", "."]
  tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py:295  assert Path(capture["cwd"]).name.startswith(".rebar-tfci-")
  tests/unit/grounding/test_terraform_corroborator.py:297  assert not any(str(repo) in arg for arg in capture["argv"])
  pytest -k subprocess_contract -> 1 passed, 24 deselected in 2.48s
  The no-leak assertion is strictly stronger now: the snapshot path is no longer in argv at all.

AC4 — the second link was independently necessary. MET.
  With the corrected schema in place and ONLY the absolute directory argument re-seeded, against
  the real binary:
    corrected schema + ABSOLUTE dir arg -> abstain / path_outside_snapshot
    corrected schema + "." dir arg      -> match / None
  So neither change alone is sufficient; the chain needed both. This is a live re-run, not a
  restatement of the earlier one.

AC5 — grounding tier green, and make verify green before push. MET.
  pytest tests/unit/grounding/ -q  ->  366 passed, 1 skipped in 207.62s (run just now at merged HEAD)
  make verify on the three-commit stack before push -> 19950 passed, 25 skipped in 31m32s,
  exit 0, zero FAILED lines.

Closing class: plan_defect. Nothing regressed and nothing was environmental — the producer
contract in terraform_config_inspect.schema.json was authored describing a tool that does not
exist (it required pos.column/pos.byte where upstream SourcePos is exactly {Filename, Line},
demanded three omitempty top-level keys, and typed resource.provider as a string where the tool
emits an object), and `_run` fed the tool an absolute directory the tool echoes back into
pos.filename. Both are errors in the original design, not in any later change or in the
environment, so the defect is in the plan itself.
